title: Chrome for Testing bar shown by default, the user's Google Chrome taken over, the keychain asked at every start
body:
## Problem

A browser started for automation must not take over the user's own browser or obstruct the view. In browser-commander 0.28.0, three things go wrong by default on macOS:

1. **Chrome for Testing shows a bar over every page:** «Chrome for Testing v156.0.8078.4 is only for automated testing. For regular browsing, use a standard version of Chrome. [Download Chrome]». It takes vertical space in every window. `--disable-infobars` (the `no-infobars` restriction) does not remove it.
2. **The user's Google Chrome is taken over:** `resolveLaunchExecutable()` prefers the installed Google Chrome (`channel: 'chrome'`). Started with another `--user-data-dir`, it is still the same app (`com.google.Chrome`) to macOS. When the user's own Chrome is not running, a click on Chrome in the Dock, ⌘T, or a link opened from another app goes to the automation window. An automation that keeps one tab then closes the user's tab.
3. **The keychain is asked again and again:** Chrome for Testing started without `--use-mock-keychain` asks «Google Chrome for Testing wants to access key "Chromium Safe Storage" in your keychain» at each start.

## Root cause and fix

1. Chromium shows the Chrome for Testing bar unless `--test-type=gpu` is given. This is the only command-line value that skips it, from `chrome/browser/ui/startup/infobar_utils.cc`:
   ```cpp
   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)
   bool IsGpuTest() {
     return base::CommandLine::ForCurrentProcess()->GetSwitchValueASCII(switches::kTestType) == "gpu";
   }
   #endif
   ...
   if (show_bad_flags_security_warnings) {
   #if BUILDFLAG(CHROME_FOR_TESTING)
     if (!IsGpuTest()) { ... ChromeForTestingInfoBarDelegate::Create(); }
   #endif
   ```
   The only other way is the `CommandLineFlagSecurityWarningsEnabled` policy. `--test-type` also skips the later infobars (session crashed, default browser, …) and does not turn `navigator.webdriver` on.
2. Launch Chrome for Testing (Playwright's or Puppeteer's), which is an app of its own (`com.google.chrome.for.testing`), and never the user's Google Chrome. The installed Google Chrome should be used only on request.
3. Pass `--use-mock-keychain` to Chrome for Testing, so the keychain is never asked. Logins moved from a Google Chrome profile can be read by Google Chrome headless, which already has access to its own keychain entry, and then set with `Storage.setCookies`.

## Requested

- A default launch restriction `no-chrome-for-testing-infobar` (`--test-type=gpu`) whenever the executable is Chrome for Testing.
- `resolveLaunchExecutable()` defaults to Chrome for Testing for automation, not to the user's Google Chrome.
- `--use-mock-keychain` by default for Chrome for Testing.
- Tests for each of these.

The hh-job-application-automation app works around this in `src/browser-session.mjs` (commit a868526 in konard/hh-job-application-automation).
